title: Al-Rashid and the Memory of the Barmecides
summary: Following the downfall of the Barmecide viziers in Baghdad, Caliph Harun al-Rashid rode through the provinces of Iraq, accompanied by his courtiers.
full_text:
Following the downfall of the Barmecide viziers in Baghdad, Caliph Harun al-Rashid rode through the provinces of Iraq, accompanied by his courtiers.

Passing through the agricultural district of Nahrawan, the Caliph stopped to admire a colossal stone bridge spanning the river, surrounded by clean irrigation canals and thriving date orchards.

The Caliph asked an elderly farmer: 'Who constructed this magnificent bridge and these canals that bring such fertility to your fields?'

The old farmer lifted his hands with tears of gratitude: 'May heaven shower blessings upon the noble house of Barmak! It was Yahya and his sons Ja'afar and Al-Fadl who built this bridge, dug these canals, and distributed seeds to the poor without demanding taxes.'

A courtier frowned and whispered sternly: 'Old man, do you not know that the Caliph has forbidden the praise of the Barmecides?'

The old farmer looked at the courtier with fearless dignity: 'You can forbid the tongues of flatterers in the palace, but can you forbid the river to flow beneath this bridge? Can you forbid the date palms to yield their sweet fruit? Every drop of water that irrigates these fields is a tongue that praises their generosity!'

Harun al-Rashid covered his eyes, wept with deep remorse, and said to his escort: 'Leave the old man in peace. He speaks truth. We had the power to destroy their palaces, but their good deeds have built a monument in the hearts of the people that will outlive our dynasty.'
moral: True statesmen who serve with benevolence leave a fragrance that royal edicts cannot erase.

quiz.question: What is the central moral lesson taught in "Al-Rashid and the Barmecides"?
options: Presence of mind and quiet wisdom triumph over brute strength.
Acting in haste and anger without thinking
Believing rumors and flattery without proof
quiz.hint: Remember the moral lesson of this traditional story.

quiz.question: How do the characters overcome their challenge?
options: Through patience, calm reflection, and wisdom
By shouting loudly and blaming others
By running away from every problem

quiz.question: What memorable conclusion does this story teach young readers?
